description: Late Iron Age - Roman settlement, site expanded greatly in the early 2nd CE, during this phase a structure defined by an enclosure was identified as a possible shrine. To the east there is another structure, this time circular, identified as a shrine. Occupation continued until at least the end of the 4th CE,
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Claydon Pike (Gloucestershire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
Smith, Alex. “The Fate of Pagan Temples in South-East Britain.” In Ritual Landsacpes of South-East Britain, edited by David Rudling, 2008.
